sections.html:
A homeowner in Eastchester may go through a broker, sell without one, or take cash. Cash tends to be quickest for a house that needs repairs or a seller who must close on a fixed day, though you should expect a figure under full market value.

First, get your tax status from the Receiver of Taxes, look up permits at the Building Department, and pin down the school district and village for the address. Price and timing both depend on those answers.

Eastchester is a town in southern Westchester County, roughly 5 miles south of White Plains and 20 miles north of New York City. It has about 4.87 square miles of land and 34,015 residents. Scarsdale lies to the north, New Rochelle to the east, Yonkers to the west and Mount Vernon to the south.

Two incorporated villages, Bronxville and Tuckahoe, sit inside the town boundaries. The rest is the unincorporated area also called Eastchester, with neighborhoods such as Lake Isle, Twin Lakes, California Ridge, Hickory Hills, Huntley Estates, Chester Heights, Garth Road and Waverly Heights. Whether a house is in a village or in the unincorporated part decides which local offices serve it, so confirm that first. Most town offices share Town Hall at 40 Mill Road.

About 72.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, the typical home value is $806,300, typical household income is $155,726 and typical monthly rent is $2,302. The average trip to work is 35.9 minutes.

Metro-North's Harlem Line stops at Crestwood, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, and the town sits between the Hutchinson River and Bronx River Parkways, with Route 22 running through the middle. Rail and parkway access is easy to verify, so give a buyer the walking distance to a station instead of a general claim.

Three school systems cover the town: the Eastchester Union Free School District, the Tuckahoe School District and the Bronxville Schools. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects the Eastchester and Tuckahoe district taxes. For a Bronxville Schools address, ask that district how its taxes are billed. Name the district in any listing.

County and town taxes are paid once a year and are due without penalty by April 30. School taxes follow a July 1 to June 30 fiscal year and are paid in two halves. The Receiver of Taxes also handles notices of tax lien sales and gives callers information on apportioning taxes in a real estate sale.

For county and town bills the cost steps up month by month: 5 percent in June and July, 7 percent in August and September, and 10 percent in the final quarter of the year.

sections.h2: What the Assessor can tell a seller
sections.html:
The Assessor estimates market value by comparing recent sales, by replacement cost, or, for rental property, by income. The first of those compares a property with similar homes that sold recently, and state law calls for every property in a town to be assessed at the same percentage of value.

Owners planning an addition or renovation can ask for a written estimate of how it would change the assessment. The request must be in writing, with drawings that mark what exists and what is new, a square footage breakdown, a narrative description and a cost estimate at market prices, even if the owner will do some of the work personally. Estimates usually arrive within a week.

Applications for senior, STAR and disability exemptions are due to the Assessor by June 1, and applicants must show Eastchester residency, so ask the office at Town Hall, 40 Mill Road, for its forms.

The Zoning Law requires many development applications to win Planning Board approval before a building permit can even be requested. Some also need review by the Architectural Review Board, the Zoning Board of Appeals if a variance or special permit is involved, or the Sign Review Board. The Planning Department staffs all four and works from Town Hall at 40 Mill Road, Room 216.

  • Comments on a hearing item must reach the Secretary to the Land Use Boards by 4:00 pm on the business day before the meeting, or be handed to the board at the hearing.
  • The Building Department, also in Room 216, takes building permit applications.
  • Town Hall is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

Before listing, find out whether any past addition or sign went through the right board, because a buyer's attorney may ask to see those approvals.

New York State charges $2 for every $500 of consideration on a conveyance, and the TP-584 return is filed with the county clerk where the property lies. Residences priced at $1 million or more also trigger a 1 percent charge that the buyer pays.

sections.h2: If you owe taxes when you sell
sections.html:
Taxes that are late carry the penalties shown in the table, and the Receiver of Taxes also handles notices of tax lien sales. Phone that office before you accept an offer and ask what is owed today, penalties included. The amount is paid out of your proceeds at closing, so it belongs in your math from the start. Write the figure down with the date you called.

A seller who is behind on the April 30 bill is usually better off selling quickly than waiting, since the monthly steps keep climbing toward 14 percent. A cash buyer will factor the balance into the offer, and your attorney will make sure it is cleared at the table.

Bring four documents to the first buyer conversation: the current tax bills, your mortgage statement, any written Assessor estimate for past work, and the approvals for additions. With those in hand a cash buyer can quote a price without a long inspection period.

The Receiver of Taxes can explain how taxes are apportioned between buyer and seller at the closing, which matters most when a sale lands between the April 30 and September 30 dates. The apportionment shows up as a line on the closing statement, so ask your attorney to walk you through it before you sign. If you plan work before selling, request the Assessor's written estimate first, so you know how the project could change the assessment a buyer will inherit.

faqs.q: Are Bronxville and Tuckahoe part of Eastchester?
faqs.a: Yes, both are incorporated villages located inside the Town of Eastchester. The town also includes an unincorporated area also called Eastchester.

faqs.q: What is a typical Eastchester house worth?
faqs.a: Around $806,300 for homes lived in by their owners. Household income in the middle of the range is $155,726.

faqs.q: When are school taxes due in Eastchester?
faqs.a: September 30 is the cutoff for the first half and January 31 for the second, both without penalty. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects for both the Eastchester and Tuckahoe districts.

faqs.q: What happens if Eastchester county and town taxes are paid late?
faqs.a: The cost rises with each month. May adds 2 percent, June and July 5 percent, August and September 7 percent, and the final quarter of the year 10 percent, with no charge through April 30.

faqs.q: Which office takes Eastchester exemption forms?
faqs.a: The Assessor's Office at Town Hall, 40 Mill Road. Exemption applications are due June 1, and applicants must show Eastchester residency.
